Adds VT sequence OSC 104 ; INDEX ST for resetting color palette entry or complete palette (if no (index is given). Adds VT sequence DECCRA to copy a rectangular area. Adds VT sequence DECERA to erase a rectangular area. Adds VT sequence DECFRA to fill a rectangular area. Adds VT sequence CSI > q (XTVERSION) to query terminal identification (name and version). Response comes as DCS >| Contour ContourVersion ST . Adds VT sequence DECRQM to request ANSI/DEC modes states (set / unset / not recognized). Adds new CLI command: contour capture ... to capture the screen buffer. Adds new CLI command: contour set profile to NAME to change the profile on the fly. Adds new CLI command: contour generate terminfo output OUTPUT_FILE to create a Contour terminfo file. Adds new CLI command: contour generate config output OUTPUT_FILE to create a new default config. Adds new CLI command: contour generate integration shell SHELL output OUTPUT_FILE to create the shell integration file for the given shell (only zsh supported for now). Also adds a pre-generated shell integration file for Linux (and macOS) to /usr/share/contour/shell-integration.zsh . Unicode data updated to version 14.0 beta. Adds support for building with Qt 6 (disabled by default). Adds support for building with mimalloc (experimental, disabled by default). 0.1.1 (2020-12-31) # Fixes race condition when displaying image animations (e.g. gifs via sixel). Fixes NewTerminal action to also inherit the active configuration file. Fixes restoring cursor position in RM ?1049 . Fixes DECSTR resetting saved-cursor state and active cursor-position. Fixes selecting text not being pushed into the selection-clipboard. Adds VT sequence OSC 7 (set current working directory). Adds VT sequence DCS $ p $Name ST to change config profile name to $Name . 0.1.0 (2020-12-24) # Available on all 3 major platforms, Linux, macOS, Windows. Emoji support (-: 🌈 💝 😛 👪 :-) Font ligatures support (such as in Fira Code). Bold and italic fonts GPU-accelerated rendering. Vertical Line Markers (quickly jump to markers in your history!) Blurred behind transparent background when using Windows 10 or KDE window manager on Linux. Runtime configuration reload 256-color and Truecolor support Key binding customization Color Schemes Profiles (grouped customization of: color scheme, login shell, and related behaviors) Clickable hyperlinks via OSC 8 Sixel inline images
docs.title: release notes

docs.text: Contour is now daemon-first: a plain contour shows sessions a daemon hosts, starting it when none runs, so closing the window no longer ends your shells. Reopen Contour, or attach from another machine over ssh or TLS, and they are still there. Set daemon: { mode: in_process } to keep sessions in the window as before.

docs.text: Adds kitty graphics Unicode placeholders (virtual placements with U=1 , placeholder cells, the a=q,e=T,U=1 feature query, and d=i/I , d=n/N and d=r/R for them) and image numbers ( I= ), so Claude Code shows its pictures, such as Mermaid diagrams, in Contour, in-process and attached to a daemon alike; until Contour is on Claude Code's list, set CLAUDE_CODE_FORCE_TERMINAL_IMAGES=1 Adds kitty graphics file media ( t=f , t=t ) for sessions whose output comes from a local program, under a strict policy: only below the temp directories and images.kitty_file_allow_list (default ~/.claude/plugins/data ), no hidden components or symbolic links, regular files the user owns with a single link; refused over SSH, in tmux panes and for daemon replicas, and switched off with images.kitty_file_transmission: false . A t=t file is deleted once read only when its path carries tty-graphics-protocol , as in kitty. Shared memory ( t=s ) is not supported Adds kitty graphics file media on Windows, at parity with Linux and macOS: below %TMP% , %TEMP% , %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp and the allow-list (default %USERPROFILE%\.claude\plugins\data ), on fixed and RAM disks only; no junctions or symbolic links below a root, no hidden or system entries, alternate data streams, device names or short 8.3 aliases; a file owned by the user (or, elevated, by Administrators) with a single link, opened so nobody writes, renames or deletes it while it is read. A POSIX path from WSL or MSYS is refused, and wsl , plink and Hyper-V's hvc count as relays On Windows, a pane now knows the program running in front of its shell (the command it runs, as Linux reports its process-group leader), so the pane header names it, closing an idle shell no longer asks first, and dropped files are quoted for the program in front Calls what you name a workspace, tab, pane or daemon its name, everywhere: contour rename OBJECT NAME names or (with an empty NAME) clears it, contour daemon --name and the daemon-service verbs name a daemon, --daemon NAME picks one on the control verbs and contour client (a local daemon's name, else a saved host's; name: and host: say which), contour switch --to-name , the SwitchToDaemon / OpenDaemon key name: , a layout tab's name: , the action RenameTab , and in the control API the name fields, object.rename , the event object.renamed (now also for tabs and panes) and the MCP tool object_rename (experimental) Gives a tab one name: Rename… in the tab strip, the sidebar or the palette sets the same name contour rename does, so a tab you renamed by hand is addressable as tab:NAME ; the tab's title stays the one its program or the title template gives it, and a typed name is taken literally, without placeholders Keeps the old spellings working until 0.9.0, each with a deprecation note: --label , contour label , contour workspace rename , switch --to-label , the configuration's label: daemon key and a layout tab's title: , the action SetTabTitle , the MCP tool object_setLabel , and the control API's old spelling ( label , object.setLabel , workspace.rename , workspace.labelChanged ), which a daemon and its clients still speak to an older peer during an upgrade Redesigns the daemon and workspace switcher (experimental) as a popup in the command palette's family, drawn in the window: it shows each workspace's status, branch and last failed command as the sidebar does, also for other daemons; typing finds workspaces on every local daemon; a daemon opens into its own level; New Daemon… checks the name as you type; workspace rows have the sidebar's right-click menu and a new-window button; it opens with Ctrl+Shift+R ( ⇧⌘R on macOS). The workspace chip's dropdown is the same popup, scoped to the window's daemon, with All daemons… to widen it Fixes emoji sequences the system's emoji font is too old to know, such as the Emoji 17.0 skin-tone variants, being drawn as their pieces far into the cells to the right: Contour now bundles Noto Color Emoji and uses it when no system emoji font draws a sequence whole, fits a sequence no font knows into its own cells, and centres an emoji a font composes from several glyphs, such as Segoe UI Emoji's families, as a whole instead of glyph by glyph (#2381) Prevents short commands from flashing the tab and desktop progress bars by delaying running and busy OSC 9;4 progress by 500 ms by default, configurable under Settings → Appearance → Tab bar (#2342) Changes the label option of contour workspace new , contour new and contour split to --name : --daemon picks the daemon on every control verb, and on these --label named both the daemon to reach and the object to make (experimental) Fixes a tab's name from contour rename tab:… NAME not being shown: the sidebar, the tab strip and the switcher now name the tab by it, as they do a workspace by its name, and show its title again once it is cleared (experimental) Fixes the status line at the top ( status_line.position: top ) having the page's first row drawn over it, and a row moving a row down while it was selected Fixes the sidebar's tab rows of a window without a daemon showing "Terminal" instead of the title the shell set, until something else changed Shows a working directory beneath your home as ~/… in the sidebar, as the pane header does, for a directory on this machine only: a path an ssh session or another machine's daemon reports is shown in full Fixes Contour on Windows ending when a terminal is resized just as its program exits Fixes inline images drawn smaller than they were sent, such as the Mermaid diagrams Claude Code renders at twice their size, looking jagged: each pixel now averages the image pixels it covers instead of picking one of them, so text and thin lines in a picture stay smooth, and transparent edges keep their colour Fixes a kitty graphics delete ( a=d ) arriving during a chunked image transmission being taken for the transmission's last chunk: as in kitty, the transmission is now aborted and the delete carried out Fixes the kitty graphics delete a=d,d=A freeing every stored image, even one never placed: as in kitty, it now frees only the images whose placements it removed, so an image transmitted for a later a=p survives it Fixes kitty graphics commands that name no image (neither i= nor I= ) being answered when they fail, which the application, expecting no reply, read as typed input: as in kitty, such a command is never answered Fixes symbols such as U+23BF and U+23F5 , which Claude Code draws its interface with, being drawn as the replacement character on Windows with strict_spacing: true : a character no configured font has is now drawn with the font Windows names for it, even a proportional one Fixes data races when a pane of a daemon session is attached: the connection's thread read which display showed the pane, and which pane the session was, while the window changed them Fixes Contour on Windows failing to save settings, load its configuration or write files with a few tabs open: each tab's fonts held files open until the process reached the C runtime's default limit of 512, which Contour now raises to 8192 (#2405) Fixes Contour on macOS and FreeBSD crashing, or no longer reading a terminal, once a process has more than about a thousand files open, as a daemon hosting a hundred or more sessions does Fixes Contour exiting at start on a Windows system without Cascadia Mono or Consolas: a missing font family now falls back to another monospace font, then to any font, and a system without any usable font is refused with a message instead of a crash Fixes a client attaching to a daemon over stdio, or a local connection, waiting forever on a daemon that never answers: the client gives up with an error after a deadline, and the daemon closes a local connection that sends nothing within 20 seconds (experimental daemon) Adds a keeper process in front of the daemon on Linux and other POSIX systems: it holds every shell's terminal and the listening sockets, so a daemon that crashes or hangs is restarted while your shells keep running, and your tabs and panes come back with them. Configure it under daemon.keeper Adds a configurable terminal type for built-in SSH profiles and falls back to xterm-256color on Windows when no terminal type is set (#2315) Adds installing Contour's terminfo entry on the remote host when a built-in SSH profile connects, so the shell starts with TERM=contour where the remote has tic , and otherwise keeps the terminal type it would have used; turn it off per profile with ssh.install_terminfo: false Adds ssh.connect_timeout , a per-profile limit (30 seconds by default, 0 for none) on how long a built-in SSH connection may take to come up, not counting the time spent waiting for a host key confirmation, passphrase or password; a host that stops answering while the connection comes up now ends it with an error instead of hanging; SSH agent authentication has its own allowance of 2 minutes Restores per-profile environment variables for local shells and built-in SSH sessions, with a Settings editor that shows each variable's name and value (#2315) Adds tab_style ( shape , spacing , material , active_fill , inactive_fill , bar_fill , active_indicator , indicator_color , tab_color_mode , close_button , new_tab_button , tab_width , min_tab_width , max_tab_width ) to restyle the tabs: their shape (the interface style's own, pill, flat, underline or outlined), the gap between them, what the bar is made of (solid, frosted or glass: Mica and Acrylic on Windows, the title bar's own material and Liquid Glass on each tab (macOS 26) on macOS, and KWin's blur on KDE Plasma), the fill of the active tab, the other tabs and the bar itself (whose labels and buttons are inked for it), a line under or over the active one and its colour, whether a tab's own colour is its fill, a tint or that line, when tabs show their close button, whether there is a "+" button, and whether the tabs share the bar equally or fit their titles, within a minimum and maximum width; also on the Tab Bar page in Settings, applied live (#2346) Adds tab_style.preset ( classic , minimal , rounded , glass , outlined ): a named look that sets the tab shape, spacing, material and fills at once; any tab_style key changed from its default still wins; also on the Tab Bar page in Settings (#2346) Animates the tab bar: a new tab fades in, the tabs beside one opened or closed slide over, and the active tab's indicator line slides to the tab made active; nothing slides when the system asks for reduced motion (#2346) Adds what runs in a tab and how its last command ended (exit status and duration, with shell integration) to the tab's hover card, and to the hover card of its row in the sidebar (#2346) Adds the profile setting tab_icon : auto shows the running program's initial in the tab's icon while a program runs, none hides the icon, and a path shows that image (PNG, JPEG, BMP, GIF, ICO or SVG); the square stays visible on a tab filled with its own colour or the accent; unlike other profile keys it is not inherited from the default profile; the sidebar's rows show it too, for the tabs the window holds; also in Settings › Profiles (#2346) Stops a program that only rewrites the host-writable status line (DECSASD), such as a prompt's clock, from marking its tab with unseen output (#2346) Fixes a sidebar row that appeared while the rows around it moved being left half transparent (#2346) Fixes dragging a tab within its own tab bar offering a drop slot where the tab already is, and past the end of the bar when it is the last tab: neither moves it, so neither is offered (#2346) Changes the Windows tab strip, under the native2026 defaults, to draw the line between two inactive tabs twice as strongly and no longer beside the active tab; configurations on the classic defaults keep the previous line (#2346) Fixes tab_bar_visibility never and multiple having no effect on Windows: the title bar now shows the window's title in place of the hidden tabs (#2346) Fixes built-in SSH profiles ignoring keystrokes after a successful login when the connection is idle (#2286) Fixes connecting to a daemon on a busy machine waiting past its connect timeout before reporting that it timed out, and reporting a connection that came up at the last moment as timed out Fixes memory corruption and crashes that program output could cause: a kitty graphics image whose declared size overflows (#2294), a character printed in insert mode right of the right margin (#2295), ICH and DECIC under origin mode with a left margin (#2296), DECCRA copying from a page of another size after a resize (#2297) and DECRQCRA for a rectangle whose corners are reversed (#2298) Fixes a ReGIS macrograph that invokes itself several times freezing the terminal (#2299) Fixes the bundled status-line extensions failing to start when built with Rust 1.100 or newer Fixes contour client occasionally crashing on Linux at startup when attaching with --connect-tcp or --host Fixes a status-line extension whose initialization never finishes hanging instead of being stopped by its load time limit, and one that calls the host while it initializes failing to start. An extension exporting another function the WebAssembly runtime would run by itself while loading it ( __post_instantiate , __wasm_call_ctors ), where no time limit applies, is refused (#2330) Fixes PNG images sent over the kitty graphics protocol ( f=100 ) not being shown: they are now decoded when they arrive (#2303) Fixes PNG images (kitty graphics f=100 , the Good Image Protocol, iTerm2 inline images) being refused in sessions hosted by a contour daemon built without the GUI, such as the contour-daemon package for servers: PNG is now decoded with libpng, a new build dependency, in every build alike; other image formats still need the GUI build Fixes control sequence numbers being taken modulo their storage size: CSI 260 h no longer sets insert mode and CSI 258 h no longer locks the keyboard (#2305), and OSC 65588 is no longer read as OSC 52 (#2304) Fixes tab stops: clearing one no longer shifts the default stops a column to the left, setting one keeps the default stops, clearing all leaves none (also in the DECTABSR report), a stop set twice is cleared at once, HT finds its stop under origin mode, and CBT from a tab stop goes to the previous one. The default stops now also reach columns the window gains later (#2309) Fixes XTPUSHCOLORS without a parameter overwriting the top of the palette stack instead of pushing, which lost the outer palette of a nested push and pop (#2310) Fixes the Good Image Protocol leaving the cursor on the image's first row when a render names a source rectangle (#2313), and ignoring the last header of a message that ends in ; , such as a release by name (#2314) Fixes built-in SSH: a host key accepted on a port other than 22 is now stored for that port only, as OpenSSH stores it, where it was trusted on every port of the host (#2306), and a long connection message can no longer be written past the read buffer (#2302) Fixes Contour terminating when closing a file descriptor fails, for instance when a signal interrupts it (#2307) Fixes tmux control mode: a layout with zero, negative or oversized pane sizes is refused instead of crashing (#2300), and send-keys sends text after -- that spells one of its own options (#2312) Fixes a daemon's client accepting screen updates whose row numbers overflow (#2308) Fixes "switch to previous tab" choosing the wrong tab after a tab was moved into another window's tab strip (#2311) Fixes a new window, from launching Contour again, contour client or New Window ( ⌘N , Ctrl+Shift+N ), showing a workspace another window already shows: it now shows the workspace no window shows that a window left most recently, so closing a window by mistake and opening a new one brings it back, or a new one. A window that loses its connection keeps its workspace for as long as it may reconnect, and one closed on purpose frees it at once Fixes Enter on a row of the workspace sidebar keeping the keyboard in the sidebar: the terminal of the row's tab or pane now takes it, as after a click Fixes a window forgetting which tab and pane were active in a workspace once it switched to another workspace and back: it now returns to the tab and pane it left Fixes the workspace chip, the switcher ( Ctrl+Shift+R ), switching by number and cycling workspaces doing nothing in a window whose sessions run in-process ( daemon: { mode: in_process } ): they now switch between that window's workspaces Fixes Contour crashing on exit when the window's sessions live in a daemon, which on macOS also started the system crash reporter beside the next launch Fixes Contour crashing when a terminal is resized just as its shell exits, for example when a window opens onto a shell that exits at once Fixes dialogs whose default button is Cancel, No or Deny drawing Trust, Yes or Allow as the default: the button Enter takes is now the highlighted one, and a destructive button that is not the default, such as Close when closing a tab, is labelled in red. Also shows the command to compare a daemon's fingerprint with in quotes instead of backticks, and no longer draws a scroll bar beside text that fits Adds a workspace sidebar: a tree of every workspace, its tabs and its split panes, each with status, reason, time and, for a workspace, its git branch with commits ahead and behind. A program that waits for you, a failure and a result you have not seen are ranked, shown and counted in its footer; ⌘J or Ctrl+Shift+J jumps to the next one, and a workspace chip marks another workspace that needs you while the sidebar is hidden. Click, double-click to rename, right-click or drag to reorder workspaces and move tabs; ⌘\ or Ctrl+Shift+B shows or hides it and ⌘⇧E or Ctrl+Shift+D focuses it; Ctrl+Alt+PageDown and Ctrl+Alt+PageUp ( ⌃⌘↓ and ⌃⌘↑ on macOS) show the next and previous workspace. A new workspace is named after its folder or repository and starts there. New configurations show it ( sidebar: { visible, width } , tab_placement: sidebar|top ); existing ones keep their tab strip. The control API gains workspace.create , workspace.rename , workspace.move , workspace.close , tab.move and pane.move . Ahead and behind are not shown on Windows yet, and the sidebar has no vibrancy or Mica Moves panes and tabs through the workspace sidebar: drag a pane onto a tab to join it as a split, onto a workspace to make it a tab there, or below the rows or onto New Workspace to give it a workspace of its own; drag a tab, or a workspace of one tab, onto the middle of another tab to merge their panes. The row menus offer the same as Move to Tab, Move to New Tab, Move to New Workspace and Merge into Tab, and contour pane move does it from the command line. The programs keep running Adds agent status for panes: Claude Code and Codex report working, needs-you and done through hooks that contour agent setup installs for each agent it finds and contour agent setup --uninstall removes. Tab badges now rank needs-you, bell, failed, done, working and unseen output, and done and failed stay shown until the pane is seen Changes a window attached to a daemon to show one of its workspaces at a time and switch between them in place, instead of opening a window per workspace: a launch opens one window, bells and notifications come from the most recently focused window, clipboard writes reach only a window showing the pane, workspace.switch asks one window, and the new NewWorkspace action creates a workspace; a daemon too old for this is refused with a hint to run contour daemon upgrade Adds the UpgradeDaemon action and the command palette's "Upgrade daemon" row, which upgrade the window's local daemon in place, keeping every program running, at any time and also when the daemon runs the same release as the client, where the drift chip offers it only for a differing release; a refusal or failure is shown as a notice Fixes a live upgrade being refused with "the new release did not answer its readiness check" when the new release starts slowly the first time, as a freshly installed one does under antivirus on Windows: the check now waits up to 20 seconds instead of 5 Fixes contour daemon upgrade , status and stop failing with "the daemon speaks protocol 4-4, this client speaks 5-5" after an update that changed the daemon protocol: these verbs now reach a daemon from before the change, so the update's own daemon can be upgraded in place, keeping its programs running Hides unavailable actions in pane and command-block menus and adds command_blocks.compact_context_menu to group a command's details and actions in a submenu or command_blocks.show_in_context_menu to omit them (#2269) Adds gutter.rail_thickness to resize or hide the rail in native UI styles. When exit-status marks are enabled, the status icon opens the command-block menu, and successful commands keep their checkmark when the rail is hidden (#2269) Changes OSC 52 to skip every byte of its data that is not base64, as xterm does, where it stopped decoding at the first one; data with no base64 in it at all is now refused rather than clearing the clipboard, where xterm clears it Fixes a rare hang when a new session, the daemon or a detached program starts: Contour no longer forks itself, which can deadlock a process that runs threads, and starts new programs through a fresh copy of itself instead Fix reversed line order when pasting multiline text on Windows (#2264) Fixes new tabs and split panes opening in the profile's initial_working_directory when the sessions live in a daemon or a tmux server: they now open in the directory of the pane they were made from, as in-process tabs do; the daemon's tmux server now honours new-window -c and split-window -c , and the control API's tab.create and pane.split inherit the calling or anchor pane's directory when no cwd is given (#2265) Adds every OpenSSH login method to ssh:// hosts: a password, a key's passphrase, a second factor, a security key's touch and the first-time host-key question are asked in a dialog of the window that started the attach, where ssh was run in batch mode and could only use a key or the agent (OpenSSH 8.4 or newer; a question a reconnect asks waits until its window is on screen and the window says "Reconnecting needs your attention") Adds signing in to a tls:// daemon with an SSH key, as ssh does: the daemon lists the public keys it accepts in authorized_keys in its configuration directory ( --authorized-keys , and --auth keys to accept nothing else), and the client signs a challenge bound to the TLS connection with a key of your SSH agent or the host's identity_file , so no secret crosses the wire. Tokens keep working with --auth any , the default, and for scripts. A key with a passphrase that is not in the agent has to be answered within the daemon's 20 seconds to sign in: load it with ssh-add first Adds pinning a daemon on first use, as ssh pins a host key: the first contact with a tls:// daemon that has no tls_ca shows its fingerprint, in a dialog that defaults to Cancel or as Trust this daemon? [y/N] on a terminal, to compare with contour daemon status , and keeps it in known_daemons ; --daemon-fingerprint settles it where nobody can be asked. A daemon that later presents another certificate is refused, never asked about, until contour daemon forget-pin HOST:PORT . The control commands no longer refuse such a daemon up front, but connect to it once it is trusted Fixes the first context or main menu freezing the window for a second or two while the speech engine listed its voices; whether speech is available is now asked on a thread of its own at startup (#2266) Adds switching a window between daemons and workspaces in place: contour switch , the SwitchToWorkspace , CycleWorkspace , SwitchToDaemon , CycleDaemon and Open… actions, --daemon NAME on every control verb, the ShowSwitcher popup that lists the daemons on this computer and the saved hosts with their workspaces, New daemon… to start another local daemon and switch to it, and a prompt that asks before a program's contour switch moves a window. A workspace you switched away from stays hidden and no launch brings it back, and attaching to a host ( contour client --host ) now brings back the workspaces nobody shows instead of mirroring every workspace of the daemon (#2253) Changes daemon mode (experimental): what a daemon holds is now called a workspace ( --workspace , --new-workspace , $CONTOUR_WORKSPACE , workspace: ids) and the old spellings ( --window , --new-window , $CONTOUR_WINDOW , window: ids) are gone for anyone who used the prerelease: an unknown option in front of a command (for example contour new --window 1 ) now fails instead of being run as the command, so pass a word that starts with a dash as -- WORD , while a dashless old spelling is no option at all and runs as the command it names ( contour new window 1 runs window 1 ); a window now means only an operating-system window. This is a breaking change to an experimental feature (#2253) Changes contour -e PROGRAM ( --execute ) to hand everything after PROGRAM to the program, options and words with dashes included, as xterm does: contour -e htop --class X runs htop --class X , so put Contour's own options before -e Fixes switching a window to a daemon no window had attached to yet (experimental) closing the window, and with it Contour: the switch now opens a new workspace there, the switcher no longer lists a workspace that holds no tab, and a window is handed its new workspace only once that holds a tab Fixes switching a window between daemons (experimental): a switch whose connection is lost before it shows its destination, or that gives up on a new workspace on another daemon, leaves that workspace hidden instead of bringing it back at the next launch; the prompt before a program's contour switch stays up only while an allowed switch can still land before contour switch stops waiting, so a window never switches after it reported a failure; and closing a window of a daemon that stopped answering no longer freezes the application for up to three seconds (#2253) Fixes switching a window to a new workspace of its own daemon (experimental) on a busy machine reporting "the daemon could not make a workspace" although the window switched to the workspace the daemon made Fixes new tabs and windows coming up in the dark color scheme on a light desktop when the sessions live in a daemon: Contour told the daemon its preference before it had read the system's light/dark setting, and the daemon builds every new session under the preference it was last told; the daemon is now told what the terminals show, and before the system's setting can be read, what they showed when Contour last ran Adds a mouse path for switching a window between daemons (experimental): clicking the host chip opens the switcher, and the Window menu lists Switch To Daemon and Daemon & Workspace Switcher… ; the switcher opens on the first local daemon that is not the window's own, counts only the workspaces that hold a tab, says connected of a saved host a window is on and not connected of one it left, and hands the keyboard back to the terminal when it closes; tabs with no title show the shell's name, or the host's name on another machine (#2253) Improves throughput of lines longer than the terminal is wide: text that wraps now goes into the grid in bulk up to the right margin and on past the wrap, where the last character of each row and the first of the next went through the per-character path (bench-headless longlines: 973 → 724 million instructions, about a quarter less) (#1488) Changes the pane, tab and workspace chords so that Shift carries: Ctrl+Alt+Arrow ( ⌥⌘Arrow on macOS) moves the focus to the pane on that side and adds Shift to swap the pane with it, Alt+Shift+Arrow ( ⌃⌥⌘Arrow ) resizes it, Ctrl+Alt+PageUp and PageDown ( ⌃⌘↑ and ⌃⌘↓ ) show the previous and next workspace and add Shift to move it up or down the list, and Ctrl+Shift+PageUp and PageDown move the active tab on macOS too ( ⌃⇧PageUp and ⌃⇧PageDown , where ⌘PageUp and ⌘PageDown no longer move it). Also moves the default chords that collided with shells, editors and IBus: full screen is F11 ( ⌃⌘F on macOS) instead of Alt+Enter , URL hints open with Ctrl+Shift+Y ( ⌘Y ) instead of Ctrl+Shift+U , which IBus takes for Unicode input, and Shift+Up , Down , PageUp , PageDown , Home and End scroll on the primary screen only, so an editor or pager keeps them; Shift+Left and Right no longer switch tabs, Ctrl+Shift+X no longer closes a pane, ⌃⇧, no longer opens Settings on macOS ( ⌘, does) and Ctrl+Alt+K and J ( ⌃⇧↑ and ⌃⇧↓ on macOS) no longer jump between prompts, which Ctrl+Up and Down ( ⌘↑ and ⌘↓ ) do. A configuration that writes out its chords keeps them. Fixes the workspace sidebar not following a reorder of a tab other than the active one, and a tab moved with the keyboard not moving in a window whose sessions a daemon hosts Adds macOS default chords: Command+P opens the command palette (Shift+Command+P still does), Command+W closes the focused pane and the tab with its last pane, Shift+Command+W closes the tab, Shift+Command+O opens the last command's output, and Control+Command+. , O, S, V and the comma toggle the status line, open the file manager, take a screenshot, paste without control characters and toggle input method handling Adds Linux and Windows default chords: Ctrl+Shift+C copies, Ctrl+Shift+W closes the active pane, Ctrl+Shift+= enlarges the font, Ctrl+Up/Down step to the previous and next command, Ctrl+Shift+Up/Down select its output (as in VS Code's terminal), and Ctrl+Shift+L clears to the prompt Changes Ctrl+Shift+Up/Down on Linux and Windows to select the previous/next command's output; Ctrl+Up/Down jump between prompts Improves soft fonts (DECDLD): glyphs now draw crisp and cell-filling at any font size, recolour with the cell's colors and reverse video, scale on double-width and double-height lines, Refuses a buffer capture in a daemon-hosted pane instead of leaving the program waiting for the reply. Draws a Linux header bar on GNOME, KDE Plasma and other Linux desktops: the tabs inline as pills, a new-tab button leading (a secondary click on it opens the profiles), search and a main menu holding the six menu-bar menus trailing, and the window's top corners rounded while it is windowed under client-side decorations Places the window buttons in the desktop's order and on its side, from GNOME's button layout, KWin's configuration or GTK's settings.ini, with close alone on the right where none is set Follows the desktop's accent colour, light or dark style, high contrast and reduced animation through the XDG Settings portal, live as they change; without a portal Contour starts as before, with the default accent Adds the ContourLinux control style, so the Settings window, menus and dialogs match the header bar; the Settings window draws its own header row with the desktop's close button Adds window_control_style: linux , the round symbolic window buttons, which auto now means on Linux, KDE Plasma included; plasma keeps the Breeze-like buttons Adds a quick terminal: a global hotkey, set in Settings › General and unbound by default, slides a terminal down from the top of the screen and hides it again, and hides it when it loses focus unless turned off; on macOS the app you came from stays in front. Adds quick_terminal ( hotkey , hide_on_focus_loss ) Shows a bell badge on a tab whose program rang the bell while out of sight, until the tab is seen; the Dock icon, the Windows taskbar button and the Linux launcher count the tabs waiting for you (OSC 7501 blocked), so a question asked in a terminal is visible from another app On macOS, a command that ran ten seconds or more in a pane you were not looking at raises a Notification Center notification when Contour runs from its app bundle; clicking it brings the pane forward with the command's block in view, and it chimes only while the bell sound is on Fixes contour help for commands with subcommands such as contour daemon : their usage lines now wrap inside the terminal width, under the command's first option, instead of running past it or indenting a subcommand's options by hundreds of columns Resizing with text reflow now respects a finite scrollback limit and releases excess history storage; infinite scrollback remains unlimited. On macOS, a Command chord that nothing is bound to is consumed instead of typing its letter, and Contour's built-in shortcuts are Command chords: ⌘C , ⌘V , ⌘T , ⌘W , ⌘N , ⌘K (clear to the prompt, on the primary screen only), ⇧⌘P and the font size on ⌘0 , ⌘- and ⌘+ , with ⌘← , ⌘→ and ⌘⌫ editing the line; the menu bar provides ⌘Q and ⌘, . Ctrl+Shift+ letter now reaches the program Adds the per-profile mouse_forwarding setting ( forwarded , the default, or blocked ) and the ToggleMouseForwarding action (View menu, command palette), which keep mouse clicks, motion and the wheel from applications that turn mouse tracking on, so selecting, scrolling and links keep working while they run; DEC locator reports and position requests follow it too, and the toggle lasts until a profile switch or a configuration reload (#2034) DEC locator button reports (DECELR) now honour read-only mode, the keyboard lock an application sets (KAM), Vi modes other than Insert, and the bypass modifier, as mouse tracking reports do; a button's release, by mouse protocol or locator, is reported exactly when its press was Fixes a ChangeProfile key binding switching to a profile named ChangeProfile instead of the one its name names With option_as_alt naming a side of the Option key, that key is Alt for every key, so ⌥B sends ESC b and Alt bindings fire; an Option key it does not name composes characters (é, ¡) and is Alt only on keys that type nothing, such as the arrows and Return. An Alt +character binding that cannot fire on a composing Option key is reported when the configuration loads (#2016) Adds the Primary modifier to input_mapping : Command on macOS and Ctrl+Shift elsewhere, so one binding is right on every platform; the generated configuration and the shortcuts shown in menus and the command palette use it On macOS, Option+arrow is sent as Alt+arrow ( CSI 1;3D ), as the keyboard protocols specify, instead of as Ctrl+arrow; ⌥← and ⌥→ move by word in the shell through default bindings outside the alternate screen On X11, the key a press types without modifiers, which the kitty keyboard protocol reports as its unshifted key, is read from the keyboard layout in use, so Shift+3 reports 3 and non-Latin layouts report their own letters; Wayland still reads it from the key's own symbol On Windows, punctuation keys are resolved through the active keyboard layout instead of being read as character codes, so a key reports the letter the layout types for it to a program using the kitty keyboard protocol: the A key on a Russian layout is ф , not a On Windows, Ctrl+Alt+click and Ctrl+Alt+wheel bindings now see both modifiers instead of losing them On macOS, the default shortcuts that conflicted with keys the system or applications expect are gone: ⌘X and ⌘S are no longer bound ( ClosePane moved to ⌘W ; SpeakSelection has no macOS default), the Alt +character defaults are desktop-only because Option composes characters there, and Ctrl+0 and Ctrl+Shift+- reach the program instead of changing the font size. The Ctrl+Alt defaults answer to ⌃⌘ instead: the stripping paste ( ⌃⌘V ), ScreenshotVT ( ⌃⌘S ), OpenFileManager ( ⌃⌘O ), ToggleStatusLine ( ⌃⌘. ) and ToggleInputMethodHandling ( ⌃⌘, ); OpenCommandOutput is on ⇧⌘O , and selecting the tenth tab ( Alt+0 ) has no macOS default. Every Ctrl+Shift+ letter now reaches the program Adds the contour-daemon package, a Qt-free .deb (Ubuntu 24.04 and 26.04, amd64) and .rpm (Fedora 44, x86_64) attached to each release, for hosting persistent sessions on a machine without a display; it conflicts with the GUI contour package, which already includes the daemon ( apt replaces one with the other; dnf refuses and needs dnf swap or --allowerasing ). It installs a systemd user unit that stays disabled until a user runs contour daemon-service install , and the packaged service opens no listening port. RPM packages come without the bundled status-line extensions; CentOS and RHEL packages are not provided yet contour daemon-service install on Linux prints a note with loginctl enable-linger when lingering is off, since the daemon otherwise stops with the user's last login session; status and uninstall now treat the service as installed only when the user registered it, not when only the packaged unit exists Brings back the Linux AppImage ( contour-VERSION-x86_64.AppImage , attached to each release): it bundles Qt 6.11, which Debian and Ubuntu do not ship, so Contour runs on a distribution whose Qt is older. CI builds it on every pull request and starts the bundle to check it Resizing no longer discards scrollback: rows a narrower or shorter window pushes past a finite scrollback limit are kept, so resizing back restores them, and the next line of output trims the scrollback back to its limit and releases the extra storage. Previously a resize either dropped them at once or let the scrollback stay above its limit for good. Fixes a taller window scrambling the screen when a finite scrollback was full: blank lines appeared mid-page and old scrollback lines showed on the page. Fixes the first scrollback trim after a resize, or on first reaching the limit, cutting through a command instead of at a prompt. Fixes a crash when widening the window while scrolled back into a long scrollback. Fixes a crash when narrowing the window after a full-screen program, such as a coding agent, redrew over a finished command's output. Fixes the next character overwriting the last one when narrowing the window while the cursor waited to wrap at the right margin, with text reflow off, on the alternate screen or with mode 2028 reset (#2123) Fixes a status-line extension started by a profile switch sometimes drawing at the wrong cell size, and keeping it, when it asked for the cell size (CSI 16 t) in its first frame Changing the window width with reflow_on_resize: false no longer walks the whole scrollback buffer, only the lines in use (#2124) Changes release tags to the bare version of the released commit, such as v0.9.0 ; the packages keep the build number as the fourth version field ( 0.9.0.9500 ), and every tag now points at exactly the commit its packages were built from Adds automatic winget updates: publishing a release now submits it to the Windows Package Manager as contour-terminal.Contour , with the per-machine and the per-user installer and the portable package; a plain winget install contour-terminal.Contour now installs for the current user, so pass --scope machine to install for all users, and the portable package stays available with --installer-type portable Prepares the Windows packages for code signing: contour.exe and both installers (and, with most certificates, its libraries) are signed once a certificate is configured, and the packages stay unsigned until then Release packages are built with link-time optimization and each platform's exploit mitigations (Control Flow Guard and CET shadow-stack compatibility on Windows; on Linux the build now sets position-independent executables, full RELRO, the stack protector and fortified C library calls itself instead of relying on the compiler's defaults) (#2250) The Ubuntu package no longer comes with a separate -dbgsym debug-symbol package; no release publishes debug symbols Adds closing a tab with a middle click on it, as in a browser Adds DECST8C ( CSI ? 5 W ), which resets the horizontal tab stops to one every 8 columns Adds CTC ( CSI Ps W ), which sets or clears horizontal tab stops: 0 sets one on the cursor's column, 2 clears it, 4 and 5 clear them all Fixes ConEmu OSC 9;9 (working directory) and OSC 9;12 (prompt start) popping up a desktop notification at every prompt: they now set the working directory as OSC 7 does and mark a prompt as OSC 133;A does Adds the answerback profile option: the message Contour replies with when an application sends ENQ (Ctrl+E). Empty by default, so nothing is sent unless configured Adds DECRSPS ( DCS Ps $ t ), which restores the cursor information (DECCIR) or tab stops (DECTABSR) an application saved with DECRQPSR Adds the xterm modes ?1036 (metaSendsEscape) and ?1039 (altSendsEscape): Alt still sends ESC before the key by default, and an application that resets both makes Alt send the key alone Fixes the cursor flickering away on almost every keystroke in a daemon session running PowerShell (PSReadLine) on Windows: the screen update that answers a key no longer goes out while the program has the cursor briefly hidden for its redraw (experimental daemon)
docs.title: Its window and Settings are redesigned to feel native on macOS, Windows 11 and Linux, with a Terminal style of their own, a command palette, command blocks, split panes with cards and a status line.

docs.text: Contour 0.8.0 turns the shell's command history into something you can see and act on: command blocks with exit-status marks, output folding, a gutter with line numbers and timestamps, a sticky command header and finish notifications, driven by OSC 133 or, on recent systemd, by OSC 3008 context tracking with no setup at all. It detects URLs and file paths in terminal output and opens them with Ctrl+click, replaces the search prompt with a GUI-native find bar, and adds kitty graphics animation frames. Terminal output throughput is up several-fold, reflow and resize keep text and the cursor where they belong, and a broad round of fixes covers Windows, Flatpak, daemon mode, SSH and the settings page.

Adds tab_color to profiles, giving newly opened tabs a default color while preserving layout, application and user overrides (#2152) Fixes closing a pane or tab keeping its session — terminal, scrollback and threads — in memory until Contour exited. A program that ignores the terminal's hangup signal is now ended 200 ms after its pane closes, as WezTerm does, and a tab no longer leaks the picture of itself it takes for the drag cursor when its window closes mid-grab
docs.title: Tabs, splits and layouts

docs.text: Adds status-line extensions (experimental): sandboxed WebAssembly modules, configured per profile under extensions , that draw an {Extension:name} segment of the indicator status line, or the whole line with status_line.extension , and are told of the pane's working directory, title, foreground process, input mode, tabs, user variables, progress, focus and font. Each pane runs its own instances on worker threads with a time limit per call and a memory cap, so a slow or failing extension never holds up the terminal; a profile without extensions starts none of it (#398) Adds the bundled extensions clock , git , sysload , agent-status and plasma (#398) Adds the run_command permission for extensions ( allow , deny or ask ): an extension runs only the commands its manifest declares, and with ask only once you allowed them; answers are remembered in extension-grants.txt , and a daemon's in a grants file of its own (#398) Adds status-line extensions to contour daemon sessions, which run them where the session lives and ask their questions in the attached client (#398) Adds remember_window_position to restore the first window’s position and monitor at startup without saving its size (#2164). Adds the global option snap_to_rows to align window heights to complete terminal rows, avoiding unused space below a bottom status line. Available in Settings and disabled by default (#2158). Adds notification_close_timeout, for the one thing the notification portal cannot do: tell an application that its notification was dismissed. Where a close cannot be observed, Contour now assumes one after this long (10 seconds by default) and reports it back over OSC 99 marked untracked , so an application that asked for close events with c=1 is answered instead of waiting forever, and can still tell a guess from an observation. A notification that states its own lifetime with w= is answered on that instead, and 0 disables the assumption entirely Extends OSC 9;4 progress indicators to the Windows taskbar, KDE Plasma launcher and macOS Dock, including while minimized, using combined progress from tabs and split panes. Changes the indicator status line to span the window's whole width: its bar reaches the window's left and right edges past the gutter and the page margins beside it, but stays its own rows' height, and its text is laid out across the gutter's columns as well as the page's, so its middle sits in the bar's centre. The host-writable status line keeps the page's width (#2139) Changes ending a shell within early_exit_threshold with a successful exit status — exit or Ctrl+D — to close the window as at any other time; the "Shell terminated too quickly" notice and its key press remain for a shell that fails, is killed, or whose exit status is unknown Changes OSC 777 and OSC 9 notifications to show only while their pane is not the focused one, as foot and Windows Terminal do, and OSC 99's o=invisible to mean while the pane is off screen: it acted as o=unfocused Fixes Windows font metrics after moving between monitors with different DPI scaling, maximized windows not filling the usable area, and resize handles remaining active while maximized or fullscreen (#2164). Fixes the Windows custom window frame growing the window and leaving a gap below the status line at startup: the client size is now preserved when the frame is applied (#2132) Fixes status-line {Command} items opening console windows on Windows and slowing down rendering: commands now run in the background at a configurable Interval= (default 10 seconds), with a 5-second timeout, and accept the {Command:<command>} shorthand (#2135) Fixes clicking an OSC 99 notification that asks for focus only raising its window: it now brings its tab and pane forward, and so does clicking a tray message off Linux. Off Linux, a notification from a pane in a background tab was dropped. In a contour client tab an application's o=always or o=invisible was lost, and OSC 99's lists of pending and shown notifications grew without limit Fixes desktop notifications never appearing in the Flatpak build. Contour asked org.freedesktop.Notifications for them directly, which a sandbox does not permit and which Flathub declines to grant a permission for; a sandboxed Contour now speaks the org.freedesktop.portal.Notification portal instead, which needs no permission at all. Outside a sandbox nothing changes — the session bus is still used, and still reports a dismissal exactly as before Fixes the window freezing for up to 25 seconds when a hyperlink, folder or configuration file is opened while the desktop's xdg-desktop-portal is not answering. Qt reaches the portal with a blocking call on the GUI thread, and since Qt 6.10 it takes that path whether or not Contour is sandboxed; Contour now speaks the portal itself, asynchronously, and falls back to xdg-open if the portal refuses. Where opening still fails, the log now says why instead of only that it did (#2075)
docs.title: Window and desktop integration

docs.text: Adds a message to the settings page that says why it refused a value or could not save a change, which screen readers announce Fixes a profile the settings page saves cutting a hint pattern's name short at " #", or no longer loading when the name holds ": "; and saving a color scheme that sets a context tint failing Fixes the Rendering GPU setting never applying, while the settings page showed it as set, when settings.yml held a hand-edited renderer: value Fixes the settings page's grapheme clustering and text scaling settings being saved but never applied Fixes number fields on the settings page storing another number than the one shown or typed: in a locale that writes a decimal comma, leaving a field that showed 0.5, such as Background opacity, stored 5, and a whole number typed with the locale's thousands separator, such as 1,000, was stored as 1. A decimal field now takes a decimal point or a comma whatever the locale, and a whole-number field takes no thousands separator Fixes a malformed entry in settings.yml or in a GUI-written profile being reported without the file's name Fixes a settings.yml or a GUI-written profile file that holds a single word aborting the load of the whole configuration. Such a file is now skipped and reported, as one that does not parse already was Fixes a settings field, switch or menu whose change was refused, or could not be saved, going on showing the refused value instead of the stored one Fixes the settings page writing an override of a global setting's value already in effect, and offering a Reset for no change, when its field was left unchanged or its menu's shown entry was picked again. Escape in a field now puts the stored value back: it kept the typed text, which the next focus change saved Fixes the settings page accepting, and saving, a PTY read buffer size of zero or less, a negative number of recent commands and a negative interface font size. It now refuses them and says why Fixes the settings page's Keybindings list showing only the first action of a binding that runs several, and leaving out the built-in bindings that contour.yml leaves free, such as Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+PageUp/PageDown switching tabs and right-click opening the context menu. They are now listed after the configured ones, marked built-in
docs.title: Command palette, settings and menus

docs.text: Adds detection of URLs, file paths (with their :line:column ) and patterns of your own in terminal output: they are underlined like OSC 8 hyperlinks once output goes quiet and open with Ctrl+click, the context menu or vi's gx , and ]x / [x move between them. Detection runs off the parser and its file checks on a thread of their own Adds link_detection to choose, per screen, whether URLs and file paths in output are detected; file paths are no longer detected on the alternate screen by default. Adds hyperlink_decoration.mode ( always , hover , modifier , never ) and makes hyperlink_decoration.normal and .hover take effect, for OSC 8 and detected links alike Adds file_opener , a command template with {path} , {line} and {column} for opening detected files, and clickable and url keys for hint_patterns ; all of them are editable on the settings page Changes hint mode's Open on a match of your own pattern whose text names no URL scheme to open nothing, as a link opens only a scheme Contour knows; give the pattern url: 'file://{0}' to open the absolute path it matches Fixes hint mode freezing on long words, ending wide-character URLs early, misplacing highlights after combining characters and cutting parenthesised URLs short Fixes a file:// link's tooltip and its click naming different files: the tooltip kept a #L10 fragment that the click dropped, and file://C:/dir was opened as the network path //c/dir Fixes Ctrl+click and hint mode resolving a relative path against a working directory that another machine reported (file://otherhost/…), opening this machine's file of the same name; in a contour client pane mirroring another machine's daemon, Ctrl+click on a file path and file:// links opened this machine's file too Fixes the status line's context breadcrumb and the hyperlink tooltip showing a right-to-left override or a control character a program sent as it was, which could reverse the rest of the status line or the link shown Fixes a link staying underlined, with its tooltip up, after the pointer left the grid for the gutter or the window's edge Fixes FollowHyperlink and OpenSelection launching what they open while holding the terminal's lock, so a slow launcher froze the terminal's output
docs.title: Hyperlinks, file paths and hint mode

docs.text: Adds search_case_sensitivity (smart, insensitive, sensitive), which the find bar's Aa button also cycles at runtime. Smart, the default, is case-insensitive until the term contains a capital, and it is Unicode-aware, so it works for non-Latin scripts (#1410) Replaces the status-line search prompt with a GUI-native find bar floating over the pane: a real text field, a live match count, previous/next, and a case toggle. Opened by Ctrl+Shift+F, or by / in Vi normal mode; neither switches the Vi mode any more. Under ui_style: terminal the same bar is drawn as a TUI — square, cell-quantized, in the terminal's own font (#2081) Changes the default auto_scroll_on_update from true to false, as in VTE, ghostty, WezTerm and Windows Terminal: a view scrolled back into the history stays there until you type. A configuration file that spells the option out keeps its value Deprecates search_mode_switch, which chose the Vi mode to return to after a search. Entering a search no longer changes the mode, so there is nothing left for it to select; the key is still accepted so existing configurations keep loading Changes {SearchPrompt} in the indicator status line to a read-only echo of the active search term, which no longer appears in the default status line Fixes a view scrolled back into the history being brought down to the bottom about once a second with auto_scroll_on_update on, while a shell that redraws its prompt in place on a timer sat idle: only output that scrolls lines into the history now brings the view down, as in ghostty Fixes search highlighting disagreeing with search matching for any non-ASCII term: the highlighter asked std::isupper, which is undefined above U+00FF, and asked it of the term's remaining suffix rather than the whole term, so "Foo" matched its tail case-insensitively Fixes being unable to edit a restored search term, and pasting into the search prompt corrupting it — both consequences of the hand-rolled line editor the find bar replaces (#1353) Fixes search and selection around double-width characters: a search missed a match running on past one, the highlight did not paint a match across one or across a soft wrap, and a double-click selected only part of a word holding one. A double-click also joined words across a hard line break, or took in the next word after a word wrapped onto a third row; vi's * and # had the same faults Fixes a fast mouse click starting a drag selection from a stale position instead of where the button actually went down, making the selected region appear to jump the moment the drag started. A slow, deliberate drag never showed this, because the pointer's tracked position was refreshed by the preceding movement; a quick click could arrive with no such movement right before it Fixes dragging out an ordinary text selection silently overwriting the active search term, so the selected text appeared as a live search wherever a status line or the find bar echoes it. Only a double or triple click's word selection is meant to do that
docs.title: Scrolling, search and selection

docs.text: Fixes permissions.capture_buffer never being consulted: a profile saying deny still raised the dialog and let the capture through once approved, and one saying allow was still interrupted by it. Both now decide the request outright, and with ask, "Yes to all" / "No to all" is remembered for the rest of the session instead of being stored and ignored (#2089) Fixes "Yes to all" on a larger-than-512-KB paste not being remembered either, so every such paste asked again Fixes a refused buffer capture leaving the requesting program hanging. The reply always ends with an empty PM 314 chunk, and a refusal sent nothing at all — so a client reading until that marker waited forever. A denial now sends the terminator, and so does a capture asked of a background pane Fixes a second buffer-capture request arriving before the first was answered being dropped, which left that request unanswered; requests are now queued and each one gets its own reply Fixes a larger-than-512-KB paste bypassing the newline normalization every smaller paste gets, so a CRLF payload arrived with carriage returns that a shell reads as Enter — under bracketed paste that executed the pasted lines instead of inserting them. Such a paste also honours the repeat count and whitespace-stripping it was asked for, and is no longer re-read from the clipboard when approved, so what is pasted is what was measured and shown rather than whatever was copied while the dialog was up Fixes pasted text ending a bracketed paste early with an embedded ESC [ 201 ~, or its 8-bit form, so that the rest reached the shell as typed keys: copying a command's output and pasting it back was enough to run what it held. ESC and C1 controls are now dropped inside a bracketed paste, and hint mode's Paste goes the same way
docs.title: Paste, buffer capture and permissions

docs.text: Changes an SSH profile that cannot connect to say so on the terminal, naming the host, the port and the reason. Every such failure — a name that does not resolve, a refused connection, an agent that is not there — used to be written only to the error log, which is off by default, so what appeared was the generic "Shell terminated too quickly." with nothing in it to act on (#2075) Changes an SSH profile under Flatpak that fails because the sandbox permits no network to say that, rather than reporting the host as unresolvable. Contour's SSH runs in-process rather than spawning ssh, so it is subject to the sandbox's own network permission; the message is chosen from what the sandbox reports it was granted, not guessed from how the call failed (#2075) Fixes contour daemon and contour client silently ignoring a profile's shell, escape_sandbox and presentation (cursor, status line, scrolling, colors) settings, hosting every session with the bare OS login shell and default presentation instead — even on the very first daemon spawn, not only when an already-running daemon was reused (#2092) Fixes contour daemon not realizing a profile's configured default_layout when it starts: it now does, so the first contour client to attach sees the real layout instead of always a single pane — including each pane's own command , arguments and directory , not just its tab/pane shape. A pane's per-tab profile override is not honored on the daemon and is logged. Fixes contour daemon retrying forever, every 100 ms, once its listening socket was gone, serving nothing and saying only that an accept had failed. It now stops accepting there and logs why Fixes ClearHistoryAndReset, SoftReset and WriteScreen in a tab attached to contour daemon acting only on the client's copy of the screen, which the next update could undo. They now run on the daemon Fixes a daemon with more than one scrollback-heavy pane becoming permanently unattachable — contour client was refused before any screen content arrived, and every reconnect failed the same way. Attach snapshots are now paced against the connection's send queue and split across frames, so attaching succeeds whatever the scrollback depth; a window resize could drop an already-attached client for the same reason and no longer does Fixes contour client never finding the daemon under Flatpak. A sandboxed daemon bound its socket under the sandbox's own $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR — a directory on a private mount the host cannot reach at any path — so a shell that escaped the sandbox had nothing to attach to. It now binds under $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/app/ , which flatpak shares with the host at the same path, and exports $CONTOUR_MUX into the shells it hosts (#2075) Fixes an SSH connection attempt skipping every other address a host name resolved to, so a host reachable only at its second address appeared to be down Fixes Contour hanging when an SSH handshake failed: the failure path took a lock the calling thread already held Fixes Contour spinning when the SSH agent could not be reached — the normal case inside a Flatpak, where $SSH_AUTH_SOCK names a host path the sandbox does not mount — instead of falling through to the next authentication method
docs.title: Daemon mode and remote sessions

docs.text: Adds Ctrl+Shift+Up and Ctrl+Shift+Down to move between command prompts on the primary screen, as in Ghostty (ScrollMarkUp and ScrollMarkDown); a full-screen application keeps the chord Fixes AltGr characters arriving on Windows as control codes: on a Swedish layout AltGr+8, 9, + and 2 typed ESC, GS, FS and NUL instead of [ ] and @. Windows reports AltGr as Ctrl+Alt, and under the Win32 input mode ConPTY enables, the character was Ctrl-mapped as if Ctrl had been pressed. A Ctrl+Alt that produced a printable character is now treated as AltGr, while a genuine Ctrl+Alt chord is still reported as one (#2127) Fixes a genuine Ctrl+Alt+key on Windows losing both modifiers outside the Win32 input mode — the case for SSH profiles: Ctrl+Alt+A typed a bare "A" instead of ESC ^A, or CSI 97;7u under the kitty keyboard protocol, and a key binding on a Ctrl+Alt chord never fired. Every Ctrl+Alt used to be taken for AltGr; only one that produced a printable character is now Fixes a key binding for BACKSLASH firing on the x key Fixes Vi mode on a page under 17 rows scrolling with every motion — j bounced the view, and H and L landed on the wrong edge — because the 8-row scroll margin was never capped. It is now capped as vim caps scrolloff Fixes Vi mode's M landing one row above vim's middle row on a page of odd height, which could scroll the page by a row, and counting the blank rows that end a page collapsed folds leave short. It now lands where vim 9.1 does
docs.title: Keyboard and mouse input

docs.text: Adds built-in drawing for more Powerline separators, including inverse dividers, thin chevrons and diagonal lines (#2160). Adds U+25BC and U+25B6 to the built-in box-drawing renderer, so they no longer depend on the font Adds renderer.gpu and a "Rendering GPU" settings entry to choose which GPU renders the terminal (Linux and Windows). The default, auto , leaves the choice to the system as before. Vulkan and Direct3D honour it with Qt 6.10 or newer; OpenGL honours it on Linux only Changes the dotted underline to be drawn as evenly spaced round dots that continue across cells. Fixes macOS configured font fallback, collection-face selection, and recovery of missing glyphs, including statusline symbols that require a proportional system fallback. Fixes Windows ignoring the configured font fallback list and switching surrounding text to another font when a glyph was missing. DirectWrite now tries the configured fonts first and only replaces missing clusters. Also fixes undersized emoji and incorrect text/emoji presentation (#2140) Fixes a combining character, such as an accent, that arrives in a separate read after a run of plain text attaching to the first character of that run instead of the last Fixes a read that ends inside a multi-byte UTF-8 character, right after a control sequence or at the start of the read, showing a replacement character in front of it and leaving the cursor one cell too far right Fixes national flags after other text pairing their letters one off: a German and a US flag written after a space showed as D, EU and S Fixes a cluster that starts with a combining mark or a zero-width character losing its first cell when the next character joins it Fixes text in a script no installed font covers rendering at roughly 3 fps: every uncovered codepoint triggered a fontconfig sort of every installed font on the render thread, and every one of those sorts returned nothing. A single probe of the union of all installed charsets now answers the same question exactly, taking the median frame from 289 ms to 12.3 ms
docs.title: Rendering, fonts and Unicode

docs.text: Adds kitty graphics animation frames ( a=f ) and frame selection ( a=a ), so applications can send only what changed between frames instead of re-sending the whole image. Animations now play on their own ( s=2 / s=3 ), with loop counts ( v= ) and gapless frames, instead of staying frozen on frame 1 (#2126). Frame payloads can be zlib-compressed ( o=z ), and frames can be composed from one another ( a=c ) (#2108). Sessions hosted by contour daemon play too, at a throttled frame rate Fixes images.sixel_scrolling: false being lost once a program reset the terminal (RIS), and never applying in a session hosted by contour daemon Fixes the kitty graphics protocol's APC payload being parsed one byte at a time through the escape-sequence state machine, where the equivalent sixel payload has long had a bulk path. An image-heavy workload's time in the parser falls from 47% of its wall clock to 6.6% — 7.55 s to 1.06 s over 1.4 GB of payload
docs.title: Images and graphics

docs.text: Adds OSC 133;N (as ;A), ;I (as ;B, for input that ends with its line) and ;L (a fresh line), the right-prompt mark ;P;k=r, and kitty's cmdline= form of the command line. A shell integration announcing commands with ;N used to get no command blocks at all, and under Nushell a command line ended in the right prompt's text (#1010) Adds PowerShell shell integration: contour generate integration shell pwsh to FILE. Like VS Code's, it wraps PSReadLine's PSConsoleHostReadLine to report the command line (#1010) Changes the bundled bash, zsh and fish integrations to report where the prompt ends (OSC 133;B) and the command line (cmdline_url), and tcsh to report the prompt end; with fish 4.0 or later, which marks its prompts itself (A, C and D from 4.0.0, the command line from 4.0.1, the prompt end from 4.3.0), the script adds only what fish leaves out (#1010) Fixes a multi-line command split into one command block per line in Nushell 0.111 and later, which integrates natively and marks each continuation line with OSC 133;A;k=s: an A carrying k=s or k=c (a continuation prompt) or k=r (a right-hand prompt) is now read as part of the prompt in progress. Nushell never reports the command line, so Contour reads it off the screen (#1010) Fixes a failed command being recorded and reported as a success when its OSC 133;D carried more parameters after the exit code, as WezTerm's 133;D;1;aid=42 does: everything after D; was read as the exit code Fixes a command line sent as OSC 133;C;cmdline_url= being cut at a raw semicolon (kitty, too, reads it to the end of the sequence); and, with a shell that sends ;C but never ;D, the prompt after a command that printed nothing (cd, true) being taken for that command's output, so screen readers found no live prompt there Fixes the tcsh shell integration on macOS printing its prompt and command marks as literal text such as \033]133;A\033\ rather than sending them: macOS's tcsh echo expands no escapes ( echo_style bsd), so the terminal saw no prompts or command blocks there Fixes the bundled bash, zsh, fish and tcsh integrations sending the working directory (OSC 7) as a raw path: a directory whose name held an escape character could send the terminal sequences of its own, such as a new window title, and a script sourced over ssh claimed a local directory. They now send a file:// URL with the host name and a percent-encoded path, and fish 4.0 and later, which sends its own, no longer gets a second one Fixes the path of an OSC 7 file:// URL being taken as written: a directory a shell announced percent-encoded, as VTE's script, fish 4 and WezTerm do, showed as /tmp/a%20b in the tab title and hint mode, and on Windows a new tab could not open in it. A new window opened in the current directory also lost the part of its path after a # or ? Fixes the bash integration installing no hooks when another copy of bash-preexec had been loaded first, as atuin and starship load it, and its hooks being replaced by a user's own functions named precmd or preexec Fixes DEC mode 2034 semantic block queries reporting a command with another command's prompt and output, or at a fresh prompt the previous command's; a shell that enables the mode from its prompt hook never seeing the command typed at that prompt; a full reset (RIS) leaving the reader's session running; and a query of an unknown type being answered as one for the last blocks
docs.title: Shell integration

docs.text: Adds output folding: collapse a finished command's output down to its prompt line and expand it again. Driven by the shell's OSC 133 marks, so any shell with shell integration works (#88) Adds a fold column in a one-column gutter left of the grid, marking each foldable block and highlighting under the pointer; clicking it, or the new context-menu entry, toggles that fold Reserves U+10F000..U+10F0FF for Contour's own glyphs and assigns the fold column's two heads, which no Unicode character describes; see docs/vt-extensions/private-use-glyphs.md Adds the global folding config section and the actions CollapseAllFolds, CollapseLastFold, ExpandAllFolds, ToggleFold and ToggleLastFold Adds a record of every command block — its command line, exit status, start time, duration and working directory — kept for the last command_blocks.max_records commands (1000 by default), even after their output has left the history (#1010) Adds exit-status coloring to the gutter's block column: a failed command's marks turn red and a running one's yellow (color scheme block_status), a running command shows ▸ and a finished one with no output ●, and hovering the column shows the exit code, duration, start time, directory and command line (#1010) Adds line numbers to the gutter, off by default: gutter.line_numbers absolute, relative or hybrid, as vim's nu and rnu. Relative distances count the lines you see, so with a block collapsed 12k still lands on the line labeled 12 (#1010) Adds per-line timestamps to the gutter (gutter.timestamps, gutter.timestamp_format): the time output first reached each line, at no memory cost per line (#1010) Adds a "⋯ 1,234 lines" label after a collapsed fold, and vim's fold keys za, zo, zc, zM and zR in Vi normal mode (#1010) Adds command marks on the scrollbar — failures, every command, and user marks (scrollbar.marks) — where clicking one scrolls to that command (#1010) Adds a sticky command header: scrolled back into a long output, the command that produced it stays pinned above it with its exit status and duration (sticky_header.mode), and once that command's own line has been evicted from the history it names the command instead, so the header never just disappears (sticky_header.show_evicted) (#1010) Adds actions on a command's output: Ctrl+triple-click selects it (SelectCommandBlock), CopyCommandBlock and CopyCommandLine copy its output or its command line (the latter safe to paste), Ctrl+Shift+G opens the last one in a pager (OpenCommandOutput, command_blocks.pager), ClearToPrompt clears everything above the current prompt, and CopySelection can fall back to the last command's output. Relative file paths in a command's output now open relative to the directory that command ran in. Ctrl+triple-click and Ctrl+Shift+G are built-in fallbacks, so they work even with a contour.yml that has its own input_mapping (#1010) Adds desktop notifications when a long command finishes where you cannot see it, on by default for commands of 10 seconds or more in an unfocused pane (notify_on_command_finish) (#1010) Adds command blocks to contour client sessions attached to a daemon: the gutter, folds, scrollbar marks, sticky header and finish notifications work there too, and reattaching never replays notifications for commands that finished while detached. OpenCommandOutput opens no pane there; bind it with placement: detached to pipe the output into a program (#1010) Adds the gutter, command-block and folding settings to the settings page. Each one overrides a single key of its section in settings.yml, and leaves the rest as contour.yml says (#1010) Adds a Command blocks group to a profile's page in the settings: scrollbar mark sources, the sticky command header and its evicted-command naming, and when, how and for which commands a finished command notifies (#1010) Adds the block-status colors (success, failure, running), the gutter-text color and the sticky-header colors to the color-scheme editor. An unedited slot keeps following the colors it is derived from and says so, and an edited one can be set to follow them again (#1010) Adds a menu for each command in the gutter: a click on a command's status mark, or a right-click anywhere beside its output, opens the context menu for that command, which can now also run it again (RerunCommand, shown and confirmed first) (#1010) Adds gutter.block_column_width , 2 by default: the fold controls and command marks are drawn across two cells at twice the size, and a click anywhere in the column lands. A failed command shows a cross, or its fold drawn heavy; the fold under the pointer is drawn bolder (gutter.bold_on_hover) in colours a scheme can set per outcome (block_status_hover), editable on the settings page; and a click on a collapsed fold's "⋯ N lines" label expands it (#1010) Adds "Copy Last Command" to the terminal's context menu, copying the last finished command's command line without the prompt in front of it; "Copy Last Prompt" copies the prompt's lines, PS1 included Adds the profile option copy_command_preserve_multiline to preserve line breaks and tabs when using Copy Command. Disabled by default. Adds history.hard_limit, which makes the scrollback evict a whole command at a time. Anything above history.limit is headroom the buffer may grow into; when it fills, entire (prompt, output) blocks are dropped from the top instead of a slice taken wherever the limit happened to fall, so the oldest line kept is a prompt with its command's output intact rather than an orphaned tail. Boundaries come from the shell's OSC 133 marks, so with no shell integration — or for a single command whose output is larger than the whole headroom — the buffer simply bounds at hard_limit and evicts line by line as before. Defaults to history.limit, which is exactly today's behaviour (#836) Changes Vi normal mode to move in visible lines, stepping over collapsed blocks; folding.on_jump_into_fold picks whether a search hit inside one expands it or is skipped Changes Vi normal mode's mm to set a user mark rather than a prompt mark: it is drawn as ◆ in the gutter and as a tick on the scrollbar, and no longer counts as a command boundary for folding or for history.hard_limit's eviction of whole commands, while [m, ]m and the im/am text objects still visit both kinds (#1010) Changes the default scrollbar.position from Hidden to Right, so the command marks on the scrollbar are visible from the start. The scrollbar floats over the terminal's edge without taking a column, appears only while there is history to scroll through, and hides on the alternate screen unless hide_in_alt_screen is turned off. The new default applies to new configurations: a contour.yml written by an earlier version keeps scrollbar.position: Hidden, because Contour writes out the full default configuration on first run, so set position: Right in the profile's scrollbar section, or pick right for "Scrollbar position" on the settings page, to see the marks (#1010) Fixes stale fold ranges after a command finished: OSC 133's ;B and ;D wrote their line flag without invalidating the ranges derived from it, so anything reading them between the end of a command and the next prompt saw the state from before Fixes CopyLastCommandOutput on output of only blank lines putting a bare newline on the clipboard
docs.title: Command blocks, folding and the gutter

docs.text: Adds support for OSC 3008, systemd's hierarchical context signalling (UAPI.15): the nested stack of contexts a shell, run0, ssh or a container runtime opens around whatever runs inside it. systemd 258 and later emit these around every interactive command with no configuration at all, so on such a system Contour learns command boundaries, exit statuses and working directories for free (#2078) Adds the {Context} indicator status-line placeholder: a breadcrumb of the contexts above the one you are typing in. It shows only privilege and machine boundaries by default and draws nothing at all when there are none, so an ordinary shell session is unchanged Adds an optional tint map to color schemes, giving the page background a different shade under an elevated, containerised, virtualised or remote context. No shipped scheme sets one, deliberately: every field OSC 3008 carries is a display hint any program on the terminal can write, so the colour is something you opt into rather than something that appears Adds fold controls, mark-jump stops and "copy last command output" to prompts without any setup on a system where OSC 3008 arrives and no shell integration is installed.
